p.t: The outside works Architect names as a model, and what it takes from each. Every entry is one the docs or code state themselves; the linked doc is where. Compiled 2026-11-03.
The rule that runs through the list is the one house-voice.md gives for Fallout: we take techniques, never text, names or assets.

rows.t: The whole lineage: text-driven, real-time, brutal and funny. Full-loot PvP, a world on a clock, the six grounded stat names, real-time cooldowns, corps, the gym that turns XP into stats, slapstick violence. Its hellcore.db LambdaMOO textdump was read as the basis for combat and stats. Hang all seven hero posters and they spell HELLMOO.

The house voice: a plain literal default, rationed stings, documents that tell the story, warm radio hosts. Fallout 2's examine texts are the length benchmark, and the docs:prose irony lint is calibrated on them.
City media, street barks and talk while the player is busy, with the volume turned down. The 0-5 star wanted level.
The comic ink look over the whole game: a screen-space outline, ink painted into textures, sharpened shadows.
The Solenne's shape: a straight tower whose floor slabs jog side to side in bands, so it reads as twisting without tapering.
The Cluster Puck League's FM soundset, an homage that copies the character and none of the assets. The vertical camera.
The default broadcast framing, high on the near side and close.
One person runs a whole team head to head, switching between skaters.
The unseen momentum meter that helps the side that's behind.
The out-the-window view: soft Mode-7 terrain, sprite trees, a hazy horizon.
The Mode-7 effect stack and sprite scaling. The cockpit reference rules out its hard racing checker.
The broadcast stage's loop: write a script, pick a set, cast it, shoot it.
The THOMAS client's triggers, aliases, timers, speedwalk, split windows and logging.
The simple comic faces on the broadcast stage.
The close-up figure's strap-wrap underwear: pale bands round the body with skin between, and bright braces. The idea only, not the costume.
The animator's mouth chart: a handful of shapes standing for all the sounds, which is what lip sync's MOUTHS are.

The Quiet Hour: an unseen voice that takes your set over and gives it back, a black-and-white picture, a story with a monster in it each night and a moral read over the end. The Horizontal and the Vertical are named for the two holds it claimed to control.
The glowing puck halo and the tail that turns red at speed.
The bestiary's one accent per enemy, after the Angels' red core; pure geometry for the Architect's own.
The fused masses as the tatarigami's writhing black flesh; eyes that carry a state, after the Ohmu; designed shadow colours, after Michiyo Yasuda.
A shape grammar per faction; rim colour set by the feeling; the street animals' neon back light.
A glow's white core with its halo shifting to cyan.
The maintenance drone's curious head tilt.
The plain-writing standard. The rules are theirs; the carve-outs are ours.
Elmore Leonard, Palahniuk, John Gardner, Le Guin's *Steering the Craft*, Chekhov, Hemingway, Vonnegut
One stated rule each: speech tags, thought verbs, psychic distance, rhythm, the gun, subtext. Vonnegut's rules are held, not counted.
The Turkey City Lexicon (Shiner and Sterling)
Names for the SF failure modes to avoid. Heinlein's dilating door, stating the strange thing flatly, is a technique to use.
Kobak et al. 2024, Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing", the EQ-Bench slop lists
Forster, Swift, Zamyatin, Wells, Voltaire, London
The prose models in "what to do instead", drawn from the library's own public-domain shelf.

p.t: The library's book texts come from Project Gutenberg, or English Wikisource where Gutenberg has no US copy, and every title must be public domain in the United States. The titles themselves are listed in systems-library.md.

p.t: The research the simulations are tuned against. Each paper is also cited where its number is used, in the linked doc or file. Only three docs keep a source list of their own: systems-fauna.md (the two starling studies), fm-sound-matching.md and game-music-craft.md.

Most of the murmuration's numbers come from the STARFLAG and COBBS reconstructions of flocks over Rome and from Hemelrijk's StarDisplay model. Code: murmur.js, murmur-gpu.js, birds.js. Doc: systems-fauna.md.

rows.t: Ballerini et al. 2008, *An empirical study of large, naturally occurring starling flocks* (
The flock's shape, 1 : 2.8 : 5.6; neighbours 0.7 to 1.5 m apart; an edge denser than the middle.
Topological neighbours: each bird follows its seven nearest, whatever the distance.
Polarisation of 0.96 and a centre moving at about 10 m/s.
Speed varies between birds by a few per cent, in smooth domains, and slowing is easier than speeding up.
Turns that start at an edge and cross the flock at 10 to 20 m/s; a bird matches its neighbours' turning (the inertial spin model).
The long axis lies 60 to 90° across the course in straight flight.
A cruise of 11 m/s, the median centre speed over 21 flocks.
Hildenbrandt, Carere and Hemelrijk 2010, Behavioral Ecology 21:1349
StarDisplay: stronger cohesion for a bird on the edge, and spacing that gives the measured neighbour distances.
Hemelrijk and Hildenbrandt 2011, *Some causes of the variable shape of flocks of birds* (
Dark bands are wings shown to the eye, so the dot is shaded by its wing plane.
Each pulse of a wave banks less than the one before.
Seen from below, a flock rolling through a turn goes lighter.
795 filmed escapes from a hawk: 1 to 6 pulses 0.86 s apart, and a hole in the flock after one attack in four.
A display lasts about 26 minutes, and murmurations peak in early February.
A starling's wingbeat, 13.3 Hz at 12 m/s.
Cutts and Speakman 1994; Portugal et al. 2014; Mirzaeinia and Hassanalian 2019, 2020
The skein: V, J and echelon shapes, spacing, station-keeping and the rotating lead.
How far off birds notice an aircraft and how late they react.
The five axes of a cat's personality: skittish, outgoing, dominant, impulsive and friendly.
The ellipsoid and round-cone estimates and the smooth union the cat is carved from, as the statue was.
Caeiro, Burrows and Waller 2017, "Development and application of CatFACS" (Applied Animal Behaviour Science)
The ear actions (forward, together, flattened, rotated, down) the ear moods are built on (EAR_MOODS).
The grid of offensive and defensive faces: an angry cat turns the backs of its ears to you, a frightened one lays them flat and down.
Smit et al. 2024, "Classifying the Behaviour of Domestic Cats using Accelerometers" (Sensors 24(8))
What a pet cat's day is: lying 37%, sitting 37%, standing 13%, eating 5%, active 3%, with the peaks at dawn and dusk, which cat-life.js weighs his day by.
The breed's head, ears, eyes, body and coat, for american_shorthair in cat-breeds.js.
CFA breed standards for the Siamese, Maine Coon, Persian, British Shorthair and Abyssinian

Each breed's build, head, ears, eyes and coat in cat-breeds.js. The Siamese is the traditional cat rather than the standard's extreme wedge, checked against photographs of seal points (Wikipedia's "Siamese cat").
Crowell-Davis, Curtis and Knowles 2004, "Social organization in the cat: a modern understanding" (Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery 6)

How cats that live together show they get on: greeting nose to nose, allorubbing, allogrooming, sleeping in contact and play; and that a household of cats has preferred associates and ones it avoids. The kinds of catMeets in cat-life.js.
van den Bos 1998, "The function of allogrooming in domestic cats" (Journal of Ethology 16)
Grooming another cat goes mostly to the head and neck, and mostly from the higher-ranking cat to the lower: the groomer in catMeets is the bossier of the two.
Reighard and Jennings 1901, *Anatomy of the Cat*

The muscle groups the cat kit's legs and body are built from and where each attaches: the triceps filling the angle behind the arm, the biceps femoris and hamstrings fanning from the point of the buttock to the stifle and shin, the calf running into the Achilles tendon.
A 19th-century engraving of a cat's skeleton drawn inside its outline, and Wikimedia Commons' "Felis catus skeleton" (a mount at Naturalis, Leiden)

Where the joints sit in a standing cat: the shoulder joint at the point of the chest, the elbow at the bottom of the ribs, the hip high under the croup, the stifle high in the flank, the high hock and the upright metatarsus. The kit's silhouette is checked by laying it over the engraving.
Müller, Wonka, Haegler, Ulmer and Van Gool, "Procedural Modeling of Buildings" (SIGGRAPH 2006)
CGA shape grammar: a mass split into floors and bays with fixed and floating sizes, occlusion queries before placing a detail, and snap lines that line up floors across masses.
A city's building interiors derived from the generated exteriors.
t3ssel8r, "Giving Personality to Procedural Animations using Math" (2022)
Second-order dynamics set by frequency, damping and response: how a cat's head, heading, speed, ears and lean follow what they're after, with the numbers set from its nature.
Miller and Allen, "GraspIt!" (IEEE Robotics & Automation Magazine, 2004)

The grasp closed on contact: every joint of a finger folds together, and as each link meets the object the joints behind it stop while the ones past it go on. How a figure's fingers close round a bottle, a phone or a deck.
Hillaire 2016, "Physically Based Sky, Atmosphere and Cloud Rendering in Frostbite" (SIGGRAPH course)
The two-lobe Henyey-Greenstein phase (forward and a weaker back lobe) and the way Wrenninge's octaves are summed off one light march.
Schneider and Vos 2015, "The Real-Time Volumetric Cloudscapes of Horizon: Zero Dawn" (SIGGRAPH course)
Powder: a thin edge seen side-on or with the sun behind you is darker than the body.
Wrenninge, Kulla and Lundqvist 2013, "Oz: The Great and Volumetric" (SIGGRAPH talk)
Multiple scattering as octaves, each with half the extinction, scattering and phase eccentricity of the last, which keeps a thick cloud bright inside.
World Meteorological Organization, International Cloud Atlas (2017 edition)
The ten genera, which deck each sits in, and the company each weather keeps: cirrostratus ahead of a front, altostratus over rain, the cumulonimbus anvil and mammatus.
Liou 1986, "Influence of Cirrus Clouds on Weather and Climate Processes" (Monthly Weather Review)
Ice crystals scatter far more strongly forward than droplets, and hexagonal crystals make the 22° halo.
Fetch-limited wave growth, because the Basin is enclosed. Pierson-Moskowitz (a fully developed ocean) was rejected.
The swell trains. A Tessendorf FFT ocean was rejected, since four readers would need it on the CPU.
Shoaling, and breaking at 0.78 of the depth.
Sun glitter from the surface slope distribution.
Absorption by colour for clear coastal water.
The comic ink edge from the depth buffer.
The materials pass, aimed at three.js's MeshStandardMaterial.
Roystan's toon shader; GPU Gems ch. 16 (wrap lighting)
The beasts' rim and the scatter band through a membrane or a slime.
Belcour and Barla; Stavenga et al. on jewel beetles
The stepped thin film on chitin, oil and glass, bluer at a grazing angle.
Helland's colour-temperature fit; UCSB dragonfish data
The burn family's blackbody ramp and the deep family's blue-green and far-red.
Catster's cat paw anatomy (catster.com, "Cat Paw Facts")
A cat's paw: four toes in an arc with a bean under each, the big pad behind them, the carpal pad up the back of the wrist and the dewclaw on the inside, on the forepaws only.
Chris Wilson, "How to Draw Cat Paws" and "How to Draw a Cat Face" (chriswilsonstudio.com)
The paw wider than the leg, its outline running on from it, the middle toes forward; the face's eyes one eye's width apart and the nose lower than you'd think.
Shell fur (Lengyel et al., "Real-Time Fur over Arbitrary Surfaces", 2001)
Fur drawn as layers over the skin, each cut down to the strands that reach it.
The 28,511-word lexicon. Its attribution has to stay in the header of formant-cmudict.js.
Klatt 1979, as used in MITalk and DECtalk
Segment durations, and the parallel formant branch.
The glottal pulse built per cycle, and the Rd voice-quality relations.
The vowels the pre-emphasis is calibrated against.
Hillenbrand et al. 1995; Nearey and Assmann 1986
The drift through a short vowel (vs, oracle-naturalness.md).
The locus equations that bend a consonant's place cue with its vowel (LOCUS_EQ).
The tracheal pole-zero pairs of a breathy voice (oracle-worklet.js).
Engel, Hantrakul, Gu and Roberts 2020, "DDSP: Differentiable Digital Signal Processing"
Training a network to play ORACLE through a differentiable copy of the worklet (oracle-neural.md).
The F0 bump at a vowel's onset after a consonant.
The break between a long subject and its verb (AUX_BREAK).
The decision trees for words the lexicon lacks (build-lts.mjs). Its CMUdict attribution stays in the header of oracle-lts.js.

The token rules ORACLE's text pass was checked against (us_text.c): money, decades, fractions, am/pm, phone numbers, ranges, units, regnal numerals (flitePasses in audio-engine.js). Rules only, no code or data taken.
The Modified Rhyme Test's 50 six-word sets (voicelab.js).
Intelligibility scoring with Whisper and a NeMo recogniser (systems-procedural-audio.md).
Yamagishi, Veaux and MacDonald 2019, CSTR VCTK Corpus (CC BY 4.0)
110 speakers' recordings to pre-train ORACLE's controller on (oracle-teacher.md).
Mehta et al. 2024, Matcha-TTS; Lyth and King 2024, Parler-TTS; Li et al. 2023, StyleTTS 2
Candidate teachers for the game's register, a later step (oracle-teacher.md).
Ito and Johnson 2017, the LJ Speech Dataset; Zen et al. 2019, LibriTTS (and LibriTTS-R)
The data under the candidate teachers, checked for licence (oracle-teacher.md).
McAuliffe et al. 2017, Montreal Forced Aligner; Kim et al. 2018, CREPE
Phone boundaries and F0 from teacher audio (oracle-teacher.md).
Phonetically balanced prompts for the teacher's text (oracle-teacher.md).
Chowning 1973, *The synthesis of complex audio spectra by means of frequency modulation*
Horner, Beauchamp and Haken 1993; Mitchell and Creasey; Caspe et al. 2022 (DDX7,
von Hippel and Huron, via Shanahan
